source_attribution: Originally authored for VIORA-DSA academic research pilot; self-contained examples verified locally with GCC.

concepts.title: Arrays, Pointer Arithmetic, and Stride Indexing
concepts.definition: A C array occupies one contiguous block of memory where indexing arr[i] computes *(arr + i), advancing by i * sizeof(*arr) bytes from the base address.
concepts.working_principle: Except inside sizeof, _Alignof, or unary &, an array expression decays to a pointer to element zero. Pointer addition scales integers automatically by the pointed type width.
algorithm_steps: Allocate N contiguous elements statically or with malloc(N * sizeof(T)).
Check NULL before dereferencing dynamic allocations.
Bounds-check every index against the tracked element count N before read or write.

time_complexity.worst: O(1) access; O(N) mid-array insert/delete shift

concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: O(1) for pointer traversal beyond O(N) stored buffer
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Requires known upper bound or dynamic reallocation; out-of-bounds pointer arithmetic past one-past-the-end is undefined behavior in C.
concepts.c_example: int sum_slice(const int *p, size_t n) { int s = 0; for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) s += *(p + i); return s; }
common_mistakes: Applying sizeof(arr) inside a function parameter int arr[], which yields sizeof(int *) instead of buffer byte length.
Dereferencing a one-past-the-end pointer (arr + N).
expected_learning_outcomes: Explain array-to-pointer decay and scaled pointer offsets.
Pass explicit lengths alongside array pointers in C APIs.

concepts.title: C Structures, Field Alignment Padding, and Pass-by-Pointer
concepts.definition: A struct groups heterogeneous fields in declaration order, inserting alignment padding bytes between fields and at the tail so each member satisfies its hardware alignment.
concepts.working_principle: Passing struct T * instead of struct T avoids copying large records across the call stack and enables in-place mutation.
algorithm_steps: Order struct fields from largest alignment (double/pointers) to smallest (char/flags) to minimize internal padding.
Pass const Struct * for read-only inspection and Struct * for mutation.
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Unordered padding creates byte holes that memcmp cannot reliably compare without zero-initializing via calloc or designated initializers.
concepts.c_example: typedef struct { int *data; size_t size; size_t capacity; } DynArray; void swap_ints(int *a, int *b) { int t = *a; *a = *b; *b = t; }
common_mistakes: Using memcmp on structs with uninitialized alignment padding bytes.
Returning pointers to stack-allocated automatic struct locals.
expected_learning_outcomes: Predict padding impact on sizeof(struct).
Prevent dangling pointers when initializing heap structs.

concepts.title: Asymptotic Time and Auxiliary Space Notation (Big-O, Theta, Omega)
concepts.definition: Asymptotic notation characterizes how resource cost f(n) scales for large n: Big-O bounds upper growth, Omega bounds lower growth, and Theta bounds tight asymptotic order.
concepts.working_principle: Drop constant factors and lower-order terms after identifying the dominant basic-operation count as a function of input size n.
algorithm_steps: Identify elementary constant-time operations and input parameters (n, V, E).
Sum loop iteration bounds and recursion tree costs.
Separate auxiliary space (extra heap/stack) from read-only input space.
concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: Measured separately from input size (e.g., O(1) iterative vs O(n) buffer/recursion depth)
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Asymptotic classes hide constant cache-locality and allocation factors that strongly affect small-n C code.
concepts.c_example: /* Two nested loops up to n without early exit => Theta(n^2) comparisons, O(1) extra space */
common_mistakes: Confusing asymptotic Big-Omega (an asymptotic lower bound on a cost function) with best-case input behavior.
Forgetting call-stack frame space when stating space complexity of recursive routines.
practical_applications: Trade-off comparisons between CPU time and RAM footprint
expected_learning_outcomes: Distinguish worst-case Big-O from best-case and tight Theta bounds.
Count auxiliary stack frames alongside explicit malloc buffers.

concepts.title: Amortized Growth in Dynamic Arrays via Capacity Doubling
concepts.definition: A dynamic array achieves O(1) amortized append cost by doubling capacity on overflow so expensive O(n) realloc/copy events occur only at powers of two.
concepts.working_principle: Across n pushes starting from capacity 1, total moved elements equal 1 + 2 + 4 + ... < 2n, yielding under 3 element writes per push on average over any sequence.
algorithm_steps: If size == capacity, compute new_cap = capacity ? capacity * 2 : 4.
Call realloc into a temporary pointer; abort cleanly on NULL without leaking old pointer.
Store item at data[size++] and increment size.
concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: O(n) capacity with load factor >= 0.5 after initial growth
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: realloc may relocate the buffer, invalidating all stored element pointers inside callers; fixed additive +k growth degrades appends to Theta(n^2).
concepts.c_example: int *tmp = (int *)realloc(arr->data, new_cap * sizeof(int)); if (!tmp) return -1; arr->data = tmp;
common_mistakes: Assigning arr->data = realloc(arr->data, ...) directly and leaking the original pointer on NULL failure.
Holding raw pointers into a growing dynamic array across push calls.
expected_learning_outcomes: Prove why geometric growth yields O(1) amortized append while linear growth yields O(n) amortized.
Implement safe realloc error handling in C.

concepts.title: Bounded Array Stack and LIFO Invariant
concepts.definition: A stack enforces Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) discipline where insertions (push) and removals (pop) occur solely at the top index.
concepts.working_principle: Maintaining an integer top initialized to -1 makes empty detection (top < 0) and full detection (top >= CAP - 1) single comparisons with zero heap allocation.
algorithm_steps: Initialize top = -1.
Push: verify top < CAP - 1, store items[++top] = value.
Pop: verify top >= 0, return items[top--].
concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: O(CAP) pre-allocated buffer; O(1) operation overhead
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Fixed-capacity stack rejects pushes when full unless backed by a dynamic array.
common_mistakes: Reading items[top] before checking underflow when top == -1.
Using post-increment vs pre-increment inconsistently between push and peek.
expected_learning_outcomes: Enforce overflow and underflow guards on stack APIs.
Replace unbounded recursion with an explicit heap/array stack.

concepts.title: Circular Ring-Buffer Queue with Explicit Count
concepts.definition: A circular queue implements First-In, First-Out (FIFO) buffering over a fixed array by wrapping indices modulo capacity.
concepts.working_principle: Tracking head and element count (rather than only head and tail) uses all CAP slots unambiguously: empty is count == 0, full is count == CAP, and tail is (head + count) % CAP.
algorithm_steps: Initialize head = 0, count = 0.
Enqueue: reject if count == CAP; write at (head + count) % CAP and increment count.
Dequeue: reject if count == 0; read items[head], set head = (head + 1) % CAP, decrement count.
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Naive array queue without modulo wrap-around wastes O(n) front slots or shifts O(n) elements on dequeue.
concepts.c_example: size_t tail = (q->head + q->count) % CAP; q->items[tail] = v; q->count++;
common_mistakes: Ambiguity between empty and full states when tracking only head == tail without count or sentinel slot.
Using signed negative indices with % instead of unsigned size_t.
expected_learning_outcomes: Implement wrap-around FIFO enqueue/dequeue without array shifting.
Distinguish full from empty states cleanly.

concepts.title: Recursion, Base-Case Termination, and Call-Stack Overhead
concepts.definition: Recursion solves an instance by reducing it toward strictly smaller base cases that terminate directly without self-calls.
concepts.working_principle: Every active invocation pushes return address, locals, and parameters onto the C call stack, so maximum nesting depth determines both stack RAM usage and overflow risk.
algorithm_steps: Check and return immediately for all minimal/degenerate inputs (e.g., n <= 1 or NULL node).
Make recursive calls strictly on subproblems advancing monotonically toward a base case.
Combine subproblem results cleanly.

time_complexity.best: Depends on recurrence branching and work
time_complexity.worst: Naive overlapping calls can blow up to O(2^n)

concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Unbalanced linear recursion of depth 10^6 can overflow typical OS thread stacks (1–8 MB) when tail-call elimination is not guaranteed in C.
concepts.c_example: static void merge_sort_rec(int *a, int *t, size_t lo, size_t hi) { if (hi - lo <= 1) return; ... }
common_mistakes: Missing or unreachable base case (e.g., unsigned underflow n - 1 when n == 0).
Recomputing overlapping Fibonacci-like subtrees instead of memoizing or iterating.
expected_learning_outcomes: Prove termination using a non-negative integer measure.
Calculate call-stack space from maximum tree depth.

concepts.title: Divide-and-Conquer Recurrences and Balanced Splitting
concepts.definition: A divide-and-conquer recurrence T(n) = a * T(n / b) + f(n) models recursive splitting into subproblems of size n/b plus merge work f(n).
concepts.working_principle: When splitting evenly in half (b = 2), recursion depth is ceil(log2 n). If each tree level does Theta(n) total work (a = 2, f(n) = Theta(n)), total runtime is Theta(n log n); if only one side recurses with O(1) combine, cost is Theta(log n).
algorithm_steps: Partition interval [lo, hi) using mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2 to avoid integer overflow.
Ensure half-open ranges [lo, mid) and [mid, hi) strictly shrink when hi - lo >= 2.

time_complexity.best: Theta(log n) single-branch; Theta(n log n) merge

concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: O(log n) stack depth; plus scratch buffers if needed
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Highly skewed pivots degrade binary partitions from O(log n) depth to O(n) worst-case depth.
concepts.c_example: size_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; merge_sort_rec(a, tmp, lo, mid); merge_sort_rec(a, tmp, mid, hi);
common_mistakes: Infinite recursion when splitting an inclusive interval [lo, hi] of length 2 incorrectly.
Computing (lo + hi) / 2 and triggering signed overflow on large ranges.
expected_learning_outcomes: Analyze recursion tree depth and per-level work sums.
Use half-open intervals cleanly to avoid off-by-one splits.

concepts.title: Singly Linked List and Pointer-to-Pointer Head Manipulation
concepts.topic: Singly, doubly and circular linked lists
concepts.definition: A singly linked list chains heap-allocated nodes where each node stores a payload and a next pointer terminating in NULL.
concepts.working_principle: Passing SNode **head lets insertion, deletion, and in-place reversal update the caller's head pointer uniformly, including when the list starts or becomes empty.
algorithm_steps: Allocate node and initialize next = *head.
Update *head = node.
To reverse: iteratively rewire cur->next = prev while preserving nxt = cur->next first.
concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: O(1) per pointer per traversal; O(n) next-pointer overhead across n nodes
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Lacks O(1) random indexing and causes poor CPU cache locality compared to contiguous arrays; freeing requires saving node->next before free(node).
concepts.c_example: while (cur) { SNode *nxt = cur->next; cur->next = prev; prev = cur; cur = nxt; }
common_mistakes: Writing free(cur); cur = cur->next; (use-after-free).
Passing SNode *head by value to push_front and failing to update caller's pointer.
expected_learning_outcomes: Update head/link pointers safely without losing tail sublists.
Contrast linked lists vs arrays on cache misses and memory overhead.

concepts.title: Doubly and Circular Sentinel Linked Lists for O(1) Unlink
concepts.topic: Singly, doubly and circular linked lists
concepts.definition: A doubly linked list links each node to both prev and next; making it circular via one dummy sentinel removes all NULL boundary branches.
concepts.working_principle: Because every node in a circular sentinel ring always has non-NULL neighbors (empty sentinel points to itself), unlinking node requires only two pointer rewrites regardless of position.
algorithm_steps: Initialize sentinel with sentinel.prev = &sentinel; sentinel.next = &sentinel.
Insert node after pos by wiring all four links before overwriting pos->next.
Unlink by setting node->prev->next = node->next and node->next->prev = node->prev.

time_complexity.average: O(1) endpoint/node splice; O(n) key search

concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: O(1) per splice; two pointers per node plus one sentinel header
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Twice the link-pointer memory of singly lists; corrupting one link direction breaks bidirectional invariants.
common_mistakes: Leaving self-loop or unlinking sentinel node itself.
Updating pos->next before setting node->next = pos->next.
expected_learning_outcomes: Eliminate NULL edge-case branches using a circular sentinel.
Perform O(1) arbitrary node removal when holding a node pointer.

concepts.title: Binary Search Tree Property and Recursive Inorder Traversal
concepts.definition: A Binary Search Tree (BST) stores ordered keys so every left-subtree key is strictly less than root->key and every right-subtree key is strictly greater.
concepts.working_principle: Searching and inserting follow one comparison per level from root to leaf; inorder traversal (left, root, right) outputs all stored keys in sorted order.
algorithm_steps: Start at root; return NULL or allocate leaf at NULL edge during insert.
Branch left when key < node->key, right when key > node->key.
Free in postorder (left, right, self) to prevent leaking child subtrees.

time_complexity.worst: O(n) on sorted insertion without self-balancing

concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: O(h) traversal stack where h is tree height (log n to n)
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Unbalanced BSTs degenerate into linked lists on monotonic input; production ordered maps use balanced trees (AVL/Red-Black). Duplicate keys require an explicit policy: reject/no-op (as in bst_insert), overwrite value, or store a multiplicity count.
concepts.c_example: if (key < root->key) root->left = bst_insert(root->left, key); else if (key > root->key) root->right = bst_insert(root->right, key);
common_mistakes: Using preorder node freeing (free(root) before freeing root->left/right).
Assuming every BST guarantees O(log n) worst-case height.
expected_learning_outcomes: Verify BST ordering invariants locally vs globally across subtrees.
Explain how monotonic inserts cause O(n) skew.

concepts.title: Array-Backed Binary Min-Heap and Sift-Up / Sift-Down
concepts.definition: A binary min-heap is a nearly complete binary tree stored compactly in an array where every parent key is less than or equal to both child keys.
concepts.working_principle: Implicit index formulas map parent(i) = (i - 1) / 2, left(i) = 2*i + 1, right(i) = 2*i + 2, allowing insertion (sift-up) and extract-min (swap last to 0 and sift-down) without child pointers.
algorithm_steps: Push: append at items[size++] and swap upward with parent while items[parent] > items[i].
Pop min: save items[0], move items[--size] to root, swap downward with smaller child until heap property holds.

time_complexity.worst: O(log n) push/pop; O(n) bottom-up heapify vs O(n log n) via n pushes

concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: O(1) operation overhead inside O(n) backing array
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Only the minimum element is directly accessible in O(1); searching arbitrary keys requires O(n) scan.
common_mistakes: Neglecting to check right child existence (c + 1 < h->size) before comparing children.
Computing (i - 1) / 2 when unsigned size_t i == 0 without guarding while (i > 0), wrapping to SIZE_MAX / 2.
expected_learning_outcomes: Derive implicit array parent/child arithmetic from 0-based indexing.
Distinguish heap-order invariant from full BST sorting.

concepts.title: Graph Representations and Breadth-First Search (BFS)
concepts.definition: Breadth-First Search explores vertices in non-decreasing hop distance from a source vertex using a FIFO queue and a visited/distance table.
concepts.working_principle: Marking a neighbor visited at enqueue time (rather than dequeue time) guarantees each reachable vertex enters the queue at most once, discovering shortest unweighted paths first.
algorithm_steps: Initialize dist[v] = -1 for all vertices; set dist[start] = 0 and enqueue start.
While queue non-empty, pop u and examine each neighbor v.
If dist[v] == -1, record dist[v] = dist[u] + 1 and enqueue v.

time_complexity.worst: O(V + E) adjacency list; O(V^2) adjacency matrix

concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Produces shortest paths only when edges have equal weight (unweighted); negative/positive weighted graphs require Dijkstra or Bellman-Ford.
concepts.c_example: if (adj[u][v] && dist[v] == -1) { dist[v] = dist[u] + 1; q[tail++] = v; }
common_mistakes: Marking visited only when dequeuing, which enqueues vertices repeatedly on dense/cyclic graphs.
Using BFS directly for shortest paths on variable-weight edges.
expected_learning_outcomes: Compare O(V^2) adjacency matrix vs O(V + E) adjacency list trade-offs.
Explain why FIFO queuing discovers minimum-edge paths first.

concepts.title: Binary Search on Monotonic Arrays and Half-Open Bounds
concepts.definition: Binary search locates a target in a sorted random-access sequence by repeatedly halving the active candidate interval [lo, hi).
concepts.working_principle: Comparing arr[mid] against target eliminates at least half of remaining elements each iteration without scanning linear prefixes.
algorithm_steps: Maintain invariant that if target exists, its index lies in [lo, hi), starting at [0, n).
While lo < hi, compute mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2.
Set lo = mid + 1 if arr[mid] < target else hi = mid (or return mid on equality).
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Requires sorted order and O(1) random access; running on unsorted arrays or singly linked lists breaks correctness or O(log n) runtime.
concepts.c_example: size_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (arr[mid] == target) return (int)mid;
common_mistakes: Writing hi = mid - 1 when hi is exclusive (or using unsigned size_t mid - 1 underflowing to SIZE_MAX when mid == 0).
Assuming sorted order without validating preconditions.
expected_learning_outcomes: Write overflow-safe, underflow-free binary search on size_t ranges.
Adapt loop exit invariants for first/last occurrence variants.

concepts.title: Stable Merge Sort via Bottom-Up / Top-Down Two-Way Merge
concepts.definition: Merge sort recursively splits a slice into halves, sorts each half, and merges two sorted subarrays in linear time while preserving relative order of equal keys (stability).
concepts.working_principle: Choosing left element on tie (arr[i] <= arr[j]) keeps equal keys ordered as originally encountered, while balanced division enforces Theta(n log n) comparisons even on adversarial inputs.
algorithm_steps: Return immediately when hi - lo <= 1.
Sort [lo, mid) and [mid, hi).
Copy merged sorted run into temporary scratch buffer using arr[i] <= arr[j] and copy back.
concepts.auxiliary_space_complexity: O(n) scratch array + O(log n) stack frames
concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Requires O(n) extra array scratch memory on arrays (unlike in-place heapsort); linked lists can merge with O(1) auxiliary node links.
concepts.c_example: if (arr[i] <= arr[j]) tmp[k++] = arr[i++]; else tmp[k++] = arr[j++];
common_mistakes: Allocating a fresh temporary buffer inside every recursive call instead of reusing one O(n) scratch array.
Breaking stability by writing arr[i] < arr[j] instead of <=.
expected_learning_outcomes: Pre-allocate a single O(n) scratch array cleanly.
Verify merge stability and worst-case Theta(n log n) guarantees.

concepts.title: Open-Addressing Hash Table with Linear Probing and Tombstones
concepts.definition: An open-addressing hash table stores entries directly inside a flat array, resolving collisions by scanning probe offsets and distinguishing deleted slots (tombstones) from never-used empty slots.
concepts.working_principle: Lookup stops immediately at HT_EMPTY, so deletions cannot write HT_EMPTY without stranding keys placed later along the probe chain; HT_TOMBSTONE bridges probes while allowing reuse on insert.
algorithm_steps: Hash key modulo table capacity; inspect slots (idx + step) % CAP.
On lookup: continue past HT_TOMBSTONE and non-matching keys; stop on HT_EMPTY or match.
On insert: track first tombstone seen; update key if found ahead, otherwise place new entry in first tombstone or HT_EMPTY.

time_complexity.average: O(1) expected at bounded load factor alpha < 0.7
time_complexity.worst: O(n) full-cluster scan or poor hash

concepts.preconditions_and_limitations: Performance degrades sharply via primary clustering as load factor approaches 1.0, requiring periodic rehash to clear tombstones and grow table size.
concepts.c_example: if (tbl[pos].state == HT_EMPTY) return -1; if (tbl[pos].state == HT_OCCUPIED && tbl[pos].key == key) ...
common_mistakes: Replacing a deleted slot with HT_EMPTY instead of HT_TOMBSTONE, prematurely terminating downstream lookups.
Inserting at the first tombstone immediately without first checking whether the same key already lives further down the probe sequence.
Applying signed k % CAP on negative integer keys in C, yielding negative out-of-bounds indices instead of casting to unsigned first.
expected_learning_outcomes: Explain why tombstones preserve probe invariants under deletion.
Analyze how load factor affects expected probe length.
